description: Coffea arabica: an evergreen shrub grown for its seeds (beans).

diseases.name: Berry Blotch
diseases.description: The berry phase of brown eye spot: dark, sunken blotches on coffee cherries.
diseases.causes: Spores spread by wind and rain; stressed, poorly fed bushes in full sun are most affected.
symptoms: Brown, sunken blotches on the cherries, often on the sunny side
Blotches turn dark and dry the pulp
Affected cherries ripen early or drop
diseases.effect: Berries lose quality and the beans can be damaged.
diseases.untreated: Losses rise on stressed, under-fed bushes.

steps.title: Remove blotched cherries
steps.instruction: Pick off blotched cherries when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Feed and shade the bushes
steps.instruction: Apply balanced fertiliser and keep some shade.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores come from leaf and berry spots.
Wind and rain carry them to the cherries.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: coffee berry blotch

diseases.name: Black Rot (Koleroga)
diseases.description: A fungal disease of coffee in very wet, shaded plantations: leaves blacken and hang from the branches on fungal threads.
diseases.causes: Spreads in long rainy spells under heavy shade; fungal threads grow along the twigs from infected leaves.
symptoms: Leaves turn dark brown to black and rot
Dead leaves hang from the twigs on white fungal threads
diseases.effect: Branches lose their leaves and berries.
diseases.untreated: Severe in monsoon areas with heavy shade.

steps.title: Remove blackened leaves and twigs
steps.instruction: Pick off blackened leaves and twigs when the plants are dry and take them away.

steps.title: Thin the shade and prune
steps.instruction: Open up the shade trees and the bush before the monsoon.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered copper product before the monsoon on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Regulate shade
prevention.detail: Not too dense in the rainy season.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on infected twigs.
In long rains its threads grow onto leaves.
Dead leaves hang on threads and spread it.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: coffee black rot

diseases.name: Brown Eye Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of coffee with round brown spots and pale centres, like eyes.
diseases.causes: Spores spread by wind and rain; worse on stressed, under-fed bushes and seedlings in full sun.
symptoms: Round brown spots with a grey-white centre
A yellow halo round each spot
diseases.untreated: Seedlings in nurseries can be badly affected.

steps.title: Remove spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Feed and shade
steps.instruction: Correct nutrition and give light shade.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Round brown spots with pale centres form.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: coffee brown eye spot

diseases.name: Coffee Leaf Rust
diseases.description: The most important disease of Arabica coffee: orange powdery rust under the leaves and heavy leaf loss.
diseases.causes: Spores spread by wind, rain and people; they need liquid water on the leaf to infect, at 21-25 °C.
symptoms: Small pale yellow spots on the upper leaf
Orange-yellow powdery spores on the underside
Spots merge; leaves drop, leaving bare branches
diseases.effect: Leaf loss cuts the next year's crop.
diseases.untreated: Severe epidemics have devastated coffee regions.

steps.title: Remove badly rusted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off badly rusted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide (copper or systemic) on the local programme on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

steps.title: Plan resistant varieties
steps.instruction: Replant with rust-resistant varieties where possible.

lifecycle: They infect through the pores underneath.
Yellow spots form, orange spores below.
Wind and rain spread new spores.
